title.en: Coordinate building systems in one coordinate model

summary: Keep structure and each service system in one shared coordinate model, and detect clashes geometrically rather than visually.
objective: Make multi-system building views informative about conflicts instead of merely colourful.
applies_when: Structure, ducts, pipes, cabling or ventilation appear in the same model.
Layers or systems can be toggled independently.
The scene claims that systems fit within a ceiling void, shaft or wall.
intent_signals: show the services in the ceiling
do the ducts clash with the beams
example_prompts: Show the ventilation, plumbing and structure as separate switchable systems.
Find where the duct runs into a beam.
negative_signals: Single-system diagrams where coordination is not in question.
Schematic riser diagrams that intentionally abandon true geometry.
not_for: Single-system diagrams where coordination is not in question.
Schematic riser diagrams that intentionally abandon true geometry.

principles: Systems only coordinate if they share one origin, one unit and one level datum. Independently authored layers that look aligned in one view are not coordinated.
Visual overlap is not a clash. Two elements can appear to cross from one angle and not intersect at all; only a geometric test answers the question.
Toggling a system is a view operation and must not delete or move anything, otherwise the coordination model changes whenever someone inspects it.
Real coordination includes tolerance: insulation, hangers, access space and installation sequence occupy volume beyond the nominal element.
implementation: Define one project origin and level datum and place every system against it; record any imported system offset explicitly at the point of import.
Give each element a system and a level so filtering is a data query rather than a hand-maintained list of objects.
Run an actual intersection test between systems and report the pair, the location and the overlap, then let the view fly to that location.
Model the service envelope, not just the pipe: add insulation thickness and access allowance where they matter.
Keep visibility state separate from the model so the clash report is independent of what is currently shown.
observable_checks: Hide and show each system in turn and confirm nothing else changes position or existence.
Introduce a deliberate intersection and confirm it is reported with a location rather than found by eye.
Check a suspect area from two different camera angles; apparent clashes that resolve with the angle were never real.
Compare the clear ceiling void against the deepest element with its allowances included.

creative_affordances: System colour coding, transparency and highlight styles are free design decisions; only the coordinate model and the test are constrained.
A schematic system diagram can accompany the coordinated model as long as the two are not confused.
known_limits: Authored coordination guidance; no clash-detection run or building model has been verified for this record.
It does not encode any building standard, service sizing rule or installation tolerance.
